title: The Tuxedo Brass Band and its players
summary: Celestin ran the brass band while Ridgley ran the orchestra; trombonists and other members are listed.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did they give cups sometimes? Like contests? A lot of people had one hander. Nice to see it. Anyway, you run those cups and all. We ripped them all. I was going to ask about the brass bands. If the tuxedo brass band marched on the street, the same fellows that played in the dance band, did you march on the street much?
Yes, I was one of the trombone players.
Were all the fellows in there? Were you manager of the brass band too?

No sir. I didn't have anything to do with the brass band. That was separate. That's Celestan. He took care of that and I took care of the orchestra. He didn't have anything to do with the orchestra, you see. So he done that to them there. Whatever was over, like a leader's shell like that, but we split on him and the job, you see, from him and I. But he didn't fool the orchestra at all, no longer when I was together. And I didn't bother with the brass band. They wanted to have to go see him.
Do you know when he organized that, was that as old as the dance orchestra or did it come up later?

The brass band? The brass band. Now, you mean the, it was along all the time we had that? Yes, is it way back? Oh yeah. It was way back then too. It was way back, the time when we organized the orchestra. Yeah, that could have been about a, a while after the auditions. It could have been around about 1970 or something like that. About that time. Yeah. Yeah, we had a good brass band and we used to put everybody on the street.
Who else played in the brass band? Did they have more than one trombone?
Yeah. You know him too, he got a leg cut up by the track. Oh, Sonny Henry.

Him and I played together, we is. Very nice color. And, uh, it's the attitude trombone, him and I. Peter Biker, Peter Biker, one of the tronettes. Celestrian was one of the tronettes. When we first started playing, let me get that thing real. When we first started playing, we were with Henry Allen over the river, you see. We all used to play with him, you see. And then we'd pull up and, you know, and I, and we'd take, I met in the other fellas to take the tuxedo bands, you see. I met in the other band. So, he was a leader, he was a leader, Peter Biker. Peter Biker, Chuck played with us. I think we had three tronettes. Lorenzo Teo, clarinet player. Eddie Jackson, played tuba. Ernest Tafani, drum. And we used, you know, later when he died, then Happy came with us. Goldstein, his name is. He came with us. And, uh, Alto was Barbarang. Barbarang. Barbarang, old man. Barbarang. I don't know what he's playing at about. No, but he's still living. I guess he's as old as you, aren't you? Yeah, I think he's a little older than me. Him and Joe Piaier, I believe, was an old Alto player. He played wrestling many times.
